executive_assessment.text: Named evidence distinguishes drought-vulnerability pockets in Southern/Kgalagadi/western Ghanzi and flood/poverty overlap around Ngamiland Delta and Francistown.

Xhumaga and Ramotswa cases show different water-access, gender and livelihood constraints. Wildlife exposure and infrastructure failures are retained without being relabelled as interpersonal violence.
Dated drought monitoring, relief options and compensation grievances identify institutional issues. Climate/social-exclusion co-location and human-wildlife conflict are not complete FCV mechanisms.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025 reports: Highest drought-vulnerability pockets are Southern District, Kgalagadi and western Ghanzi; Ngamiland Delta subdistrict and Francistown combine high flood risk with many poor households.
Source dated 2025 reports: In Ngamiland East, smallholders use hybrid seeds, changed planting and water harvesting; access to credit remains a barrier to investment.

Source dated 2025 reports: Kalahari communal pastoralists are disproportionately affected by land privatization; Ngamiland, Chobe and Central combine high climate impacts with social exclusion, whose reported drivers include process-legitimacy and social-cohesion challenges.

Source dated 2025 reports: The CCDR says women's water-collection and natural-resource roles heighten climate exposure; Bogakhwe knowledge, drought-tolerant crops and livelihood diversification support adaptation, while female-headed households in Kweneng show resilience and women report less institutional confidence.
Source dated 2020 reports: The plan's 2015 assessment found over 50% precipitation shortfalls in parts of Ngamiland, Ghanzi and Kgalagadi; other high-risk areas had 25-50% deficits.

Source dated 2010-10 reports: The plan says drought concentrates people and wildlife around remaining water points and identifies the Boteti River as an existing Makgadikgadi human-wildlife-conflict focus.

Source dated 2010-10 reports: At Gweta, Phuduhudu, Rakops and Mmatshumo, focus groups said low or late compensation left farmers bitter toward wildlife and government; the plan judged direct compensation ineffective as appeasement.

Source dated 2022-08-25 reports: In Xhumaga beside Makgadikgadi National Park, drought dried the seasonal river; a broken boundary fence and failed backup borehole left people and elephants sharing water, amid crop damage and reported trampling.

Source dated 2022-08-25 reports: Xhumaga women responsible for household water collection were especially exposed to human-wildlife conflict shifts; households had little capital for climate-adaptive planning.

Source dated 2022-08-25 reports: Ramotswa households had more formal employment and livelihood diversity, and greater capacity to withstand drought and flood shocks than Xhumaga, but faced dry taps, billing, maintenance and outage barriers.

known_gaps.text: No inspected primary source establishes climate-driven armed violence or intercommunal violence in Botswana, or armed conflict disrupting adaptation delivery. The best-supported FCV pathway is drought/climate stress interacting with human-wildlife conflict, livelihood losses and retaliatory risk; these are not equated with armed conflict.
The 2010 Makgadikgadi plan and 2022 Xhumaga-Ramotswa study are location-specific and dated. The 2025 official HWC briefing is national and not locally disaggregated.
The 2020 National Drought Plan cites a 2015 risk map and proposed actions for 2020-2023; later plan implementation and current monitoring capacity were not verified.
The 2025 CCDR combines staff risk overlays and referenced studies of different vintages. Its co-location of climate impact and social exclusion does not establish a climate-caused conflict pathway.
A September 2026 peer-reviewed Boro/Okavango climate-conflict article was located, but its publisher full-text page returned 403. No claim was taken from the indexed abstract.
Human-wildlife conflict is not equated with FCV. No complete source-supported climate-to-interpersonal/armed-conflict or reverse-FCV pathway is assembled.
Dated compensation grievances and co-located social exclusion warrant sensitivity in programme design but do not establish a climate-caused conflict chain.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
